title: Academy Evaluations Hub
tagline: Evaluations and attendance hub integrated with the GPS platform
problem: Evaluation calendars, attendance and compliance for 6 departments lived scattered — and the new hub had to consume GPS/wellness data already processed by the existing platform without duplicating pipelines or creating a second write source.
targetUser: Academy technical staff and departments (U15/U17 categories).
myRole: Sole developer: data modeling, API, UI and integration.
process: Full-stack Next.js (App Router) + TypeScript + Tailwind app with Drizzle ORM. Two persistence implementations behind per-domain facades (calendar, players, evaluations, compliance): SQLite for local dev, managed PostgreSQL for production — switched by a single environment variable. Integration through a shared database: the hub reads sessions/wellness read-only; the GPS platform remains the only writer of that data.
keyDecisions: Single writer per data domain: GPS/wellness belong to the existing pipeline; the hub only writes evaluations/calendar (own prefixed tables).
Per-domain facades: same UI and API run on SQLite or the managed database with no code changes.
Canonical athlete name shared across systems — the whole integration hangs on that convention.
Calendar with chained blocks (one event per date+category) and 4-state attendance.
result: MVP + integration implemented: day panel, month/week calendar, athlete profile with integrated GPS+wellness panel, weekly compliance per area, per-department CSV import, and athlete sync from the GPS platform registry (a hundred-plus athletes synced).
learned: Integrating two systems through one database only works with explicit ownership rules — who writes what, and a shared identity key agreed before any code. Environment boundaries matter too: one production variable dropped into the neighbor system's .env broke its local dev — the rule is now documented in the file itself.
